claims.claim_text: The energy shock from the Iran conflict is a real but delayed economic negative whose full demand-destruction impact has not yet appeared in US data, creating false confidence in equity markets.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: An energy/oil shock occurred around the Iran conflict threatening the Straits of Hormuz; initial market panic sold off through March but quickly reversed in early April when the worst-case didn't immediately materialize.
Step 2: Markets interpreted the absence of an immediate collapse as the absence of any shock, leading to a re-risk rally — but this misunderstands the long-and-variable-lag nature of energy shocks.
